title: Batching-collector memory bloat incident - runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working runbook draft for incidents where the background component we call the 'batching-collector' (responsible for accumulating microbatches for continuous batching and maintaining per-tenant KV prefixes) slowly grows resident memory, eventually triggering host OOMs and sometimes causing batch-queue deadlocks when eviction stalls. The doc captures detection signals, immediate triage steps, temporary mitigations we used in the Feb 12 incident, and proposals for a long-term fix and alerting.

Why this is different from other KV/eviction notes: the failure mode here is not a single crash or a KV index corruption; it is progressive heap amplification inside the collector that correlates with a particular client workload pattern (many short-lived streaming requests with repeated small prefixes) plus a regression in the collector's flush path introduced in runtime PR #3126. The collector can end up holding many tiny slices in memory and never releasing them because of a missed async-completion callback window.

Impact observed (Feb 12, 2025, cluster: us-east-2):
- ~8 hosts across serving-pool-3 experienced host-level OOM kills within a 90 minute window.
- Tail p95/p99 generation latency for affected tenants jumped from 120ms/320ms to 700ms/3.2s.
- Several microbatch queues entered a state reported as "stalled" for >30s in the tracing UI.
- No model inference correctness regressions observed; failures were availability-only.

Detection signals (what alerted us):
- Host OOM v2 alert fired (host oom count > 1 in 5m).
- Batch-queue stalled > 30s alert (new SLI) tripped for two routes.
- Memory alloc churn on collector process (proc.mem.rss) trending up for >45m and not decreasing after GC cycles.
- Error spike: "collector: flush async callback timeout" logs.

Initial triage timeline (abbreviated):
- 2025-02-12 10:42 UTC: Pager triggers (oncall: maya). Slack thread: #ops-serving-runtime.
- 10:44 UTC: Confirmed host OOM kills; prioritized mitigation.
- 10:50 UTC: Check deploys — no recent deploys to serving runtime in last 48h except PR 3126 (rolled 2025-02-10).
- 11:02 UTC: Memory heap samplings collected (pprof) show collector heap dominated by ~small slice objects (~48–80B) pinned by pending promise objects.
- 11:18 UTC: Rolling restart of collectors on affected hosts started (graceful drain + host restart).
- 11:35 UTC: Restarts reduced memory pressure; OOMs stopped but two hosts still showed intermittent queue stalls.
- 12:10 UTC: Scoped rollback of PR 3126 to canary showed no recurrence on canary hosts.
- 13:00 UTC: Emergency hotfix PR created to ensure timeouts force-complete pending flush futures; merged and rolled to affected pool.
- 13:45 UTC: System stabilized.

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
1) Regression in async flush path introduced by PR 3126 changed how flush promises are reused. Under a workload of many tiny streaming prefixes, a rare race allowed a promise to be orphaned and the collector to keep references to transient buffers.
2) Because the collector maintains per-tenant in-flight maps, the orphaned entries accumulated until host memory pressure triggered OOM.
3) As eviction logic attempted to run it sometimes reacquired locks in an order that caused batch-queue stall / apparent deadlock (locks: collector-map -> eviction-queue mutex).

Immediate mitigations (what to do when this happens):
- Escalation and communication
  - Notify #ops-serving-runtime and the impacted customers (CS/AE) with the incident tag. Use template: "collection-memory-bloat incident: hosts affected, mitigation in progress, ETA for stabilization: 30–90m".
- Short-term runbook steps (order matters):
  1) Identify affected hosts: query metrics for proc_mem_rss for process 'collector' > 70% of host memory in last 30m. Command (internal): `infra-metrics query "proc.mem.rss{svc="collector",host=~"serving-pool-3.*"} > 0.7 * host.mem.total"`
  2) If >2 hosts affected, prefer rolling restart rather than immediate host reboot. Drain traffic: `rh-ctl drain-host --service collector --host $HOST` then `systemctl restart collector`.
  3) If deadlock detected (batch-queue stalled metric), check for lock owner stacks: `sre-stack-dump --pid $(pidof collector) --filter locks` and look for "collector-map" -> "eviction-queue" order.
  4) If stack dumps show orphaned promises/pending flush > 5000 entries, escalate to eng-serving-runtime and consider targeted rollback of recent commits (list the commits in linked_artifacts).
  5) Increase collector flush tight-timeout (temporary dynamo config): `dynconfig set collector.flush.timeout 150ms` to force completion of stale futures. This avoids long-lived references until a code fix lands.
  6) If eviction is saturated, temporarily disable background prefetch for affected pool: `rh-ctl set-config serving-pool-3 prefetch.enabled false` (risk: increased cold-start latency).

On-call checklist (short actionable):
- Check host oom alerts.
- Check collector.proc.mem.rss per host and look for monotonic growth over 30m.
- Cross-check deploy log for PRs in last 72h.
- Try drain + restart collector on 1 host; observe whether process memory resets.
- If restarts stabilize: keep rolling restarts until pool healthy, schedule full rollback/patch.
- If restarts not stabilizing or OOMs continue: escalate page to ENG-SERVING-RUNTIME (pager oncall).

Post-incident permanent fix proposals:
- Fix PR: ensure flush future lifecycle is robust (the hotfix we merged is a bandaid; rewrite to use per-flush unique ids and safe reclamation). Owner: Ethan Liu (ENG-SERVING-RUNTIME). Jira: SRE-4289.
- Add bounded per-tenant in-flight limits with backpressure: cap pending flush entries per tenant at 2000 and reject new prefixes with HTTP 429 to avoid unbounded memory. Owner: Ravi Patel.
- Improve eviction lock ordering: change eviction to use try-lock with backoff instead of blocking hand-over-hand to reduce deadlock risk. Owner: Lina Gomez.
- Add GC-friendly pooled-buffer strategy (avoid tiny allocations per request). Owner: Platform infra.

Observability and alerting changes (to add before next release):
- New metric: collector.pending_flush_count per host and per-tenant. Alert if > 2000 per tenant or > 50k cluster-wide.
- Expose heap sampled object-size histogram for collector; alert on sudden shift to many small object buckets.
- Dashboard tile: host map of collector.rss / host.mem.total with trending.
- Add trace spans for flush promise lifecycle; sample 1% of flushes for full lifecycle traces.

Runbook steps to land (action items):
- QA: Add synthetic workload that mimics many small streaming prefixes to regression tests. (Owner: Eng QE).
- Release: Coordinate rollback test harness to quickly revert PRs in canary. (Owner: Release Eng).
- Documentation: Update per-pool emergency flags and explain tradeoff of disabling prefetch. (Owner: SRE Docs)

Open follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- SRE-4289: collector flush lifecycle rewrite — owner: Ethan Liu — ETA: 2025-03-14.
- SRE-4290: bounded in-flight per-tenant with backpressure — owner: Ravi Patel — ETA: 2025-03-28.
- Dashboard work: collector pending_flush_count + heap histograms — owner: Sofia Martinez — ETA: 2025-03-07.
- Postmortem writeup + blameless RCA — lead author: Maya Chen — draft due 2025-02-25, final by 2025-03-04.

Notes to reviewers / TODOs: (these are loose notes, keep italicized bits in the doc until resolved)
- Need to confirm whether any customers saw corrupted outputs or retry loops increments. Early signals show no correctness issues but double-check logs per-tenant.
- Consider whether dynconfig changes (flush.timeout) should be defaultable per-customer tier.
- Evaluate impact of per-tenant 429s on high-QPS customers — coordinate with CS before enabling aggressive backpressure.

Appendix: useful commands and links
- List recent serving runtime deploys: `git log --since='72 hours' --pretty=oneline origin/main -- services/serving-runtime`
- Stack dump helper: `sre-stack-dump --service collector --host $HOST > /tmp/stack-$HOST.txt`
- Memory profiling: `pprof -http=:6060 http://$HOST:6060/debug/pprof/heap` (requires tunneling for prod).
- Temporary dynconfig commands (internal): `dynconfig get collector.flush.timeout --pool serving-pool-3` then `dynconfig set collector.flush.timeout 150ms --pool serving-pool-3`
- Slack channel: #ops-serving-runtime (pinned incident templates).

End of draft. Please add any missing troubleshooting commands, confirm owners, and move to in_review when the hotfix and dashboards are merged.
